key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (at least 10% and more frequent than placebo) were somnolence, dizziness, fatigue, diplopia, and headache. In the pooled trials, at 400 mg/day somnolence occurred in 37% (vs 11% placebo) and dizziness in 33% (vs 15% placebo). The most serious risk is DRESS/multiorgan hypersensitivity (three cases in development, including one fatality); other notable risks are QT shortening and dose-dependent CNS adverse reactions.

summary.text: Cenobamate (Xcopri), a new molecular entity, was submitted November 21, 2018 and approved November 21, 2019 for treatment of partial-onset seizures in adults, supported by two adequate and well-controlled placebo-controlled trials. It was reviewed as a standard NDA under section 505(b); it was not referred to an advisory committee, and no accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, or orphan designations are stated in the documents.
